doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Country club dates and Art Ford's TV show
summary: Tony Cabot society dates, and Marty's weeks on Art Ford's show ending over hiring advice.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: during the night would say “Now we’re going to have — Marty’s going to bring some guys out” and we would get on the floor and do a little bit. People went crazy. So now another country club says hey why don’t we have a New Orleans type of — get that Marty. I did loads of those things. Not only that, I did about ten or twelve weeks on Art Ford’s Channel 13 show, which was coming from Newark, and the only reason they called was because we were at the Metropole, they got most of their guys from the Metropole. Now Art Ford, the kind of music he liked was like Zutty Singleton, George Wettling, what they called “moldy fig” kind of music. Do you know what that is? You know, traditional jazz, the old. Zutty with the [scats] and all that kind of stuff. And now this girl that was hiring the musicians for the thing, she didn’t know this much about who to hire. She didn’t know any musicians at all. So when she met me, she would talk to me and say who should I get? I said well man there’s so many guys around, come on. So I would give her a list of names and it went along pretty good until one time when he had already hired Buster Bailey on clarinet and I had recommended guys like Sammy Most, Tony Scott, Gerry Mulligan, Morgana King, these are like a different era, these are not like old fashioned Dixieland. So now we’re doing a show and there’s Buster Bailey and Sammy Most. Do you know Sammy Most? Now Sammy’s a fantastic player, but he doesn’t play like Buster Bailey and vice versa. So what happened was on the show, after the show, he went to the girl and he says, “who the hell hired this guy?” No he said, “why did you hire this kid on clarinet?” She said, “Well Marty said—” he said, “Marty said? Who’s running this show, Marty or me?” That was the last time I played on it. So that was it. I said thanks a lot. But anyway she used to call my house to get information about who to hire, and my kids used to say, “Dad it’s her again.” They knew she was going to be on for three hours. All right now listen Red Allen plays well with Buster Bailey and J.C. Higginbotham, Charlie Shavers plays well with anybody. And tell her who plays well with who. Did you ever see it—
Please write it down so that you don’t have to keep calling back again and again, too, right?
This woman. You know I’ve had people do that over and over.

Well she didn’t know. She was well intentioned, she was a nice lady, I liked her, but I used to go, “don’t you know — didn’t you ever hear of Gerry Mulligan?” Anyway, so now who else did I say after that, the Metropole?
